statistics.evidence_quote: As of March 2026, the United States had 94 operating commercial nuclear reactors at 54 nuclear power plants in 28 states.
statistics.denominator_definition: EIA-described operating commercial reactors and plants, as of March 2026; a plant can contain multiple reactors.
statistics.footnote: The source separately notes that operators report Palisades and Crane as operating but “out of service” in the EIA generator survey. Neither this count nor the capacity inventory proves those plants resumed generation.

milestones.achievement: Vogtle Unit 4 entered commercial service, completing the two-unit AP1000 expansion.
milestones.remaining_gate: Commercial service is achieved; continued licensed operations and fleet performance remain ongoing obligations.
milestones.evidence_quote: Vogtle 4 entered commercial service on April 29 to wrap up the power plant’s expansion project in Waynesboro, Georgia.

milestones.achievement: DOE announced closing a $1.52 billion loan for restoration and restart of the existing 800 MW Palisades plant.
milestones.remaining_gate: The cited financing page makes restart subject to NRC licensing approvals; a loan close is not resumed generation.
milestones.evidence_quote: In September 2024, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced the closing of a $1.52 billion loan to Holtec Palisades, LLC (Holtec Palisades)

milestones.achievement: Palisades ceased operations; subsequent restart work is an existing-plant restoration rather than a new reactor build.
milestones.remaining_gate: Reauthorization, plant readiness and demonstrated return to generation must be verified separately.
milestones.evidence_quote: The plant, which ceased operations in May 2022, will be brought back online and upgraded to produce firm baseload power until at least 2051, subject to U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) licensing approvals.

gaps: Historical year-end power-plant site counts for 2021–2025 were not verified; omitted rather than backfilled from a current snapshot. March 2026 plants are a separate dated observation.

The undated EIA industry page reports 98,441 MW near its March 2026 inventory, while MER reports 96,880 MWe for year-end 2025. They have different reporting frames and cannot be silently substituted. The industry page notes Palisades/Crane operating-but-out-of-service reporting.
MER defines operable as holding a full-power license or equivalent permission, including long non-routine shutdowns. It is not an instantaneous online count.
Capacity factors are the EIA-published time-adjusted series, sourced from Table 7.8a, and are not recomputed from year-end licensed-unit capacity.
2026 is incomplete; no 2026 annual generation or annualized partial-year estimate is supplied.
Direct NRC restart project/release fetches were blocked. Search excerpts provide discovery leads only; no claim of Palisades or Crane resumed generation is included.

A discovered DOE Vogtle Unit 3 announcement URL returned 404. Its commercial-operation date was not newly asserted from a snippet; the parent repository already holds a separate company-source history.
EPA annual index release date was verified, but MER is the reproducible single-series numerical baseline retained here. No mixing of revised figures from different releases.
